title: Quadlet: allow configuring name template for secondary units
body:
### Feature request description

Healthchecks fail on my system. I default-deny most of what `systemd-analyze security` checks for and allow services minimal capabilities and system calls. This is only manageable because systemd looks up overrides by left-truncating each unit's name: `foo-bar.service` gets overrides from `foo-.service.d`. This permits me to remove restrictions from all systemd- units, for example. Because podman needs a great deal of access to configure containers, I name all quadlets with a `quadlet-` prefix and override most restrictions.

Podman creates new units to perform health checks using the systemd API. These are named `<container id>-<some hex>.service`. The prefix is essentially random so I can't grant permissions to these. The service never reaches a healthy state, systemd always shows failed units, and the journal gets cluttered. 

### Suggest potential solution

I would like a way to configure the name of these secondary units. Maybe like `<quadlet name>-healthcheck.{service,timer}`. That would get the same overrides the quadlet itself gets. For example, if I have `quadlet-collabora.service` the healthcheck could be `quadlet-collabora-healthcheck.service.d`, which would get overrides in `quadlet-collabora-.service.d` and `quadlet-.service.d`.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I could turn off default denials but given all the recent zero days I think they're pertinent.

I could use SELinux instead. That is a major undertaking for my server. But even if I do enable SELinux I think default denials are another useful layer.

I could scope the denials and prefix *all* the units on my system, but there are many vendor units I don't want to rename.

I could add drop-ins inside *every* unit on my system but it's easy to slip up and leave a service unrestricted.

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.
